featured_reviews.review_text:
Passport Seva Kendra Malad– Detailed Experience Review

Appointment & Arrival
My reporting time was 9:15 AM and appointment time 9:30 AM. I reached the location around 8:30 AM, which helped a lot since there were only two people ahead of me.

---

Location & Accessibility

The centre is located in a busy market area with street vendors and vegetable sellers near the entrance, so the surroundings feel crowded. However, accessibility is good and the location is not far from the Western Express Highway.

---

Parking

Parking is available for passport applicants in the basement of an adjacent building. I was able to park my car easily, probably because I arrived early. Security guards near the parking area are helpful, though they do tend to ask for tips (I ended up giving ₹20 each). Capacity for parking is unclear, so early arrival is advisable.

---

Process & Timeline

The overall process is systematic but involves multiple steps:

1. Entry & Photocopy Counter
Since I arrived early, I was allowed inside earlier than my reporting time. The first step was a photocopy counter where I had to buy a ₹4 Tatkal undertaking form.

2. Token Counter
Documents and originals were checked, and a token was issued.

3. Counter A
Documents were scanned and uploaded, and the photograph was taken. Once uploaded, documents become accessible across Counters A, B, and C.
Staff here (likely privately recruited) were professional and polite.

4. Waiting Area → Counter B
After Counter A, applicants wait until their token appears on the screen. Counter B mainly verifies originals; in my case, very little interaction happened. The govt employee should have checked my originals. He just let me go to Counter C where queries were raised

5. Counter C (Final Approval)
This is the final approval stage handled by a gazetted officer.

---

Staff Experience

Counter A staff were professional and courteous.
Staff at Counters B and C (government employees) were noticeably less polite and less helpful. Interaction felt rigid and somewhat dismissive.

One important observation: despite alternative documents being listed on the passport website, acceptance seemed to depend heavily on officer discretion.

In my case:

I had a registered rent agreement as address proof.
The officer demanded a bank passbook as photo ID, which I had not carried.
My company photo ID (from a public listed company), although listed as acceptable online, was rejected.
Digilocker documents were also not accepted despite broader government policy supporting them and paperless bharat.

This makes the experience feel unpredictable and somewhat dependent on individual officers.

---

Overall Experience

The process was quick — I finished and exited by around 9:45 AM, which is impressive timing. However, I had to go back and forth between counters due to document preferences and verification issues.

**Pros**

* Fast processing when slots are less crowded
* Parking availability
* Organized digital workflow at Counter A

**Cons**

* Crowded surrounding area
* Informal expectation of tips near parking
* Inconsistent document acceptance
* Mixed professionalism across counters

All the best

featured_reviews.review_text:
Good experience here! The management is great, and the employees are cooperative.

featured_reviews.name: Wandering Postcard
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited PSK Lower Parel for my passport renewal & the entire process was incredibly smooth.  I reached 30 minutes early but the staff checked my details & allowed me in right away. At the gate itself, I was guided on the first step to take. At the document quality check counter, I took a while to find my papers. The officer politely asked me to step aside so the next applicant could proceed without delay which I appreciated.  There is a small photocopy counter inside if you miss any document & they accept both cash & GPay. Once you get your token number, you are directed to the booth for document submission & biometrics. After that, there are two more verification steps at separate counters. You will need to wait for your token to be called.  The wait can be long & mobile network is poor inside. However, staff are helpful & friendly & also there is a snacks & coffee counter to keep you going.  Overall, well organized & efficient.

featured_reviews.name: suyog soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
1. An appointment is mandatory to visit the Passport Seva Kendra; without one, you will not be allowed entry.
2. The PSK at Lower Parel is a 15-minute walk from Prabhadevi Station. You will also be able to get a taxi.
3. If you wish to come by car or bike, good paid parking facilities are available here.
4. The PSK at Lower Parel is located just behind the IKEA building.
5. After entering the IKEA building gate, you must go straight, and the PSK office is located on your left side.
6. After receiving the token, it may take 45 to 75 minutes for the passport processing.
7. Keep a photocopy of all the original documents along with it.
8. The staff is very nice and cooperative.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant More
featured_reviews.review_text: Just visited the passport office and gotta say, the new staff are RESCUING the day! Fast and smiling. Skip the hassle, use Gate No 4, Trade View Building, Utopia City, Pandurang Budhkar Marg, Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: Anjali S
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the passport office today for the renewal of my child’s passport. While the initial process was simple, the waiting time has been extremely frustrating. I arrived at 12:30 PM and have been waiting for counter C since 1:15 PM.
The staff strength seems very low. Only two staff members are actively working, while others appear to be on leave or taking extended breaks. I also observed staff from Section C moving around in Section B and engaging in casual conversations instead of attending to applicants. This lack of focus only adds to the delays.
It is especially difficult for children to wait for such long periods under these conditions.
About five years ago, when the center was managed by Tata, the service was smooth and efficient. Unfortunately, the current experience is disappointing and feels like a waste of time.
Additionally, for the past hour, only Tatkal applicants are being attended to. It is unfair to make normal applicants wait indefinitely. Proper management should ensure both categories are handled efficiently.
Overall, the process needs improvement in staffing, supervision, and applicant prioritization to avoid causing inconvenience to families.

The absolute highlight had to be our time in Kruger. We stayed at the luxurious Radisson, where we could see Impalas from the room balcony! Back in Cape Town, we explored the Cape Winelands, enjoying private tastings at iconic estate - Stellenbosch. The sunset cruise around the Cape Peninsula was unforgettable - we even spotted some playful seals and penguins! Between activities, we stayed at absolutely gorgeous hotels, which honestly felt more like living in luxury homes than hotels.

What made everything extra special was Neha's personal touch and attention to details. She isn't just knowledgeable about travelling - she's passionate about it. She knew exactly what she was doing and crafted an memorial experience.

If you're dreaming of exploring South Africa, you absolutely need to check out Passport Paradise. They've nailed the perfect mix of luxury and authentic local experiences. I'm already planning my next trip with them ! 🦁✨
